questions.e: P(white) = 1/2 P(red) means 4 white balls, 12 in all. Red then white without replacement: 8/12 × 4/11 = 32/132 = 8/33.
questions.s:
A bag contains 8 red balls and some white balls. If the probability of drawing a white ball is
half of the probability of drawing a red ball then find the probability of drawing a red ball
and a white ball if the balls are drawn without replacement.

questions.e: Of 36 outcomes, totals 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 occur 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15 times. Probability = 15/36 = 5/12.
questions.s: Two dice are tossed. What is the probability that the total score is a prime number.

questions.e: p * 2 = 2p + 2p + 2 = 4p + 2 and p * 1 = 2p + p + 1 = 3p + 1. Their difference is p + 1 = 40, so p = 39.
questions.s: If p * q = 2p + pq + q, find p  when ( p * 2) - (p * 1) = 40

questions.e: With replacement: P(both red) = (7/11)^2 = 49/121 and P(both black) = (4/11)^2 = 16/121. Same colour = 65/121.
questions.s:
A bag contains 7 red and 4 black identical balls. Two balls were picked at random from the
bag and replaced each time. Find the probability the two balls were of same colour.

questions.e: Grapes or bananas = 6 + 11 = 17 out of 30 fruits. Probability = 17/30.
questions.s:
In a basket of fruits, there are 6 grapes, 11 bananas, and 13 oranges. If one fruit is chosen
at random, what is the probability that the fruit is either a grape or a banana?

questions.e: Even numbers on a die are 2, 4, 6: three of six outcomes. Probability = 3/6 = 1/2.
questions.s: Find the probability of getting an even number in a single throw of a six-sided die.

questions.e: The events are independent, so one person dying (q) and the other surviving (p) has probability q × p = pq. If either person could be the one who dies, this doubles to 2pq.
questions.s:
If the probability of death is q and the probability of survival is p, find the probability of one
death and one survival in an accident involving two persons

questions.e: Ripe pears = 100 − 20 = 80. Probability = 80/100 = 4/5.
questions.s:
Out of 100 pears bought from the market, 20 are unripe. What is the probability that the
pear picked is ripe?
